newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan seen affected by April trading.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan seen affected by April trading.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc's second-quarter earnings may show the impact of a difficult trading environment in April, analysts said Wednesday.
"They had a real good first quarter in trading which didn't carry over," said one analyst who declined to be identified.
Analysts differed on exactly what the impact would be.

"My sense is that the consensus estimate of $1.95 per share would be a bit challenging," said Judah Kraushaar of Merrill Lynch, referring to the First Call mean. He said he was using an estimate of $1.90 per share at the beginning of the quarter and did not think earnings would come in much less than that.
Kraushaar stressed that it was early June and the second quarter had not yet ended.

Still, he said April was a challenging month in the capital markets, marked by confusion over the debate in Washington on a balanced budget deal. Under the circumstances there was some impact on both customer business and proprietary trading.
Earlier, analyst George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison said J.P. Morgan might miss the $1.95 consensus by $0.20 to $0.25.
A spokesman for J.P. Morgan said the company does not comment on earnings estimates.
J.P. Morgan earned $2.04 per share in the 1997 first quarter.
